## Best Choice: Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5

**Why it wins for your use case:**
- **16 GB RAM** is the biggest practical advantage for coding tools plus many browser tabs.
- **1 TB SSD** gives you much more room for projects, datasets, apps, and photo files.
- **Ryzen 7 8845HS** is the strongest performance option here for multitasking and light editing.
- **14-inch FHD+** is usually easier on battery than a very high-resolution panel, which helps for long study sessions.
- At **$949**, it stays comfortably under budget while offering the most headroom.

**Trade-off:** the screen is not as sharp as the Acer’s 2.8K panel, so it may be a little less crisp for text and photos.

## How the Other Two Stack Up

**Acer Swift Go 14**
- Best if you want a **sharper 2.8K screen** for reading, coding, and photo work.
- Also has the right **16 GB RAM** and a very light body.
- Slightly weaker value than the Lenovo because it only gives you **512 GB SSD** and costs almost the same as the MacBook.

**MacBook Air 13 (M2)**
- Best battery life and the lightest option.
- Great for portability and long reading sessions.
- The main issue is **8 GB RAM**, which is a real compromise for coding, many tabs, and photo editing in 2026-era workloads.
- Good choice only if you strongly prefer macOS and do not multitask heavily.

## Quick Recommendation

- **Best overall:** **Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 5**
- **Best display:** **Acer Swift Go 14**
- **Best battery/portability:** **MacBook Air 13**, but only if 8 GB RAM is acceptable
